ref.title: Measures and temperatures
ref.intro: Temperatures, ratios, times and cuts from every lesson in one place. Tap a row to open its lesson.
ref.tempsNote: Measure in the thickest part, not touching bone. Pull it 3–5°C early: meat keeps cooking while it rests.
ref.restText: Steak 5 min, roast 10–15 min, loosely covered with foil.
ref.zoneText: Between 5°C and 60°C bacteria multiply fastest. Cool cooked food and refrigerate it within 2 hours.
landing.title: Learn to cook. And to think like a chef.
landing.sub: A step-by-step cooking school from a chef with 16 years in professional kitchens. Exact measures, a sign that tells you it is done, and the reason why.
landing.how1d: One action, up to 15 words. The phone sits by the board and the screen stays on.
landing.how2d: 5 mm, 74°C, 8 min. Never "a little" or "medium heat".
landing.how3d: A sign you can see, hear or feel. You confirm it instead of guessing.
landing.how4d: Every lesson ends with a "why". After grade 1 you cook without a recipe.
landing.chefRole: Chef · 16 years in professional kitchens · runs 4 restaurants in Belgrade
exam.label: Final exam
exam.intro: You open the fridge and find 10 ingredients. Plan a meal, write down three decisions, cook it and check yourself. No recipe.
exam.rules1: One plate: a protein, a side and vegetables.
exam.rules2: You do not have to use everything in the basket.
exam.rules3: Salt, pepper, oil and flour are always there.
exam.planIntro: Write a sentence or two for each decision. This is a cook's thinking, not a recipe.
exam.cookIntro: While you cook, tick each habit as you do it.
exam.doneText: You cooked a meal without a recipe and you know why you did every step.
exam.macro: Enter this meal in MacroChef as a recipe and see the macros of your own dish.

mode.theoryText: The whole lesson on one page: steps, drawings, the why and the mistake everyone makes.
mode.practiceText: Step by step at the stove. The screen stays on and timers start with a tap.
practice.title: Before you start
practice.l1: Put everything from “You need” on the counter.
practice.l2: Stand the phone next to the board so you can see it without touching it.
practice.l3: The screen will not turn off while you are in the steps.
practice.l4: Yellow buttons with a clock start a timer. The phone beeps when time is up.
practice.tip: Theory first? Read the lesson, then come back.

mode.t2: Drawings, measures and the why for every step
mode.t3: At the end: the mistake everyone makes and a check

landing.pain1: You follow the recipe and it comes out nothing like the photo.
landing.pain2: You can't tell when the meat is done, so you leave it a bit longer, just in case.
landing.pain3: The fridge is full, but without a recipe you don't know what to cook.
landing.painAnswer: The problem isn't you. A recipe tells you what to do. This course teaches you why.
landing.quote: I've spent sixteen years in professional kitchens, and I teach every new cook in the same order: knife and heat first, then taste, and only then dishes. This course is that same path, written step by step, for your kitchen.
landing.faq1a: No. Grade 1 starts with how to hold a knife and where raw meat goes in the fridge.
landing.faq2a: Each lesson is 5–10 minutes of reading. You cook at your own pace, no deadlines.
landing.faq3a: A good knife, a board, a frying pan, a saucepan, a pot, a thermometer and a scale. It's all explained in the first lesson.
landing.faq4a: Serbian, English and Russian. Switch with one tap, any time.
landing.faq5a: Yes. Install it on your phone and it works in the kitchen without signal.
landing.finalTitle: Your first cut is five minutes away.
landing.finalText: Open the first lesson, get your knife and board, and start.

oops.crash.title: Something got burnt.
oops.crash.text: We pulled the pan off the heat and opened a window. Your progress is safe, just start again.
oops.crash.cta: Clean the pan and carry on
oops.missing.title: This dish isn't on the menu.
oops.missing.text: The page you are looking for doesn't exist or has moved. The kitchen is still open.
ask.title: Ask the chef
ask.empty: Ask anything about cooking or the lesson you have open: ingredient swaps, what to do when something goes wrong, how long, at what temperature.
ask.placeholder: E.g. what can I use instead of shallots?
ask.note: Answers come from AI and can be wrong. For food safety, the measures in the lessons apply.
ask.error: The answer did not come through. Try again in a moment.
ask.offline: No internet. Questions need a connection; the lessons work without one.
ask.limited: Too many questions at once. Wait a minute and ask again.
ask.notConfigured: The assistant is not switched on yet. Coming soon.
ask.refused: I can't answer that one. Ask me something about cooking.
